info.title: Dev Health Auth Control Plane v1
info.summary: Wire contract for the Go Auth Control Plane service.
info.description:
OpenAPI 3.1 description of the Auth Control Plane v1 wire surface.

WHY 3.1 AND NOT 3.0: OpenAPI 3.1 uses JSON Schema draft 2020-12 as its schema dialect directly, so the `$ref`s below point at the SAME schema files the Go, Python and TypeScript validators read. OpenAPI 3.0 uses a modified subset of draft-04 and would have required a second, translated copy of every schema -- and two copies of one contract is the drift class the cross-language golden fixtures exist to catch.

WHY JSON AND NOT YAML: this document is validated by three runtimes. JSON needs no parser beyond the one each already has; YAML would add a parser dependency to the Go and TypeScript sides purely for the sake of convention, and a document that is harder to check is not a better contract.

PATHS: the four session routes auth-service mounts when its session secrets are set (CHAOS-10228): POST /v1/token/refresh, GET /v1/sessions/current, POST /v1/sessions/revoke and POST /v1/sessions/revoke-all. With neither secret set the service mounts only the retryable 503 stubs of the refresh and logout routes of go-api, the well-known routes when a token issuer URL is set and the workload exchange when it is on, and answers 404 on every other path. Each path has a row in contracts/auth/v1/endpoint-profiles.auth-service.json; POST /v1/authorize and POST /v1/authorize:batch, the policy decision point, are served when AUTH_AUTHORIZE_CALLER_SUBJECTS and a token issuer URL are set; the paths of later routes land with those routes.

post.summary: Decide one authorization request for a user principal
post.description: A policy-enforcement point asks whether the principal named by principal_reference may take an action on a resource. The answer is an authorization_decision.v1, allow or deny. The reason_code is for the policy-enforcement point and is not to be echoed to an end user. Every state read of the call runs in one read-only transaction.

The body is one of the two, never both.

post.summary: Decide up to 100 authorization requests in one call
post.description: As authorize, for up to 100 requests. Each request is decided apart: one deny never changes another decision. The answer holds one decision per request index. A refused principal_reference or a state failure on any request fails the whole call.

post.summary: List the repositories a user principal may read in one organization
post.description: A policy-enforcement point asks which repositories the principal named by principal_reference may read in one organization through acr.context.read or acr.evidence.read. The request is one authorization_request.v1 whose resource is {type repository, key *, organization_id}. The answer is one authorization_decision.v1, the set of repositories the per-key read decisions of that action allow: an allow carries obligations.repository_scope organization (every repository) or obligations.repository_allowlist, the principal's own canonical repository keys (at most 256, [] for none); more than 256 keys is the deny repository_allowlist_too_large, never a truncated list. No repository catalog is read and no decision cache is used. Every state read of the call runs in one read-only transaction.

get.summary: Start an OAuth 2.1 authorization request (RFC 6749 section 4.1.1)
get.description: Pre-session: the route accepts no credential. It checks the client registry, the exact redirect_uri, PKCE S256 and the RFC 8707 resource, writes one request row and redirects the browser to web's consent page with the request id only. After the redirect is proven, an error goes to it as error, state and iss (RFC 9207). Unreachable from outside while go-api's AUTH_PROXY_OAUTH is off.

302.description: To web's consent page with request_id, or to the client's exact redirect with error, state and iss

400.description: Either the request body could not be read (a transport failure within the size limit), answered by the transport before the route in its own error envelope, transport-error.v1; or the route's own error.v1 refusal with reason malformed before the redirect is proven (an unknown client, a metadata client, an inexact redirect, an unset web origin or resource): no Location. The body is one of the two, never both.

post.summary: Describe, approve or deny an authorization request, from web's server side
post.description: Under the web session's access token. A form body: action describe binds the request to the bearer's web session once and returns the client and the consent anti-CSRF token; approve or deny needs the same session and principal and that token, and answers the redirect web sends the browser to.

200.description: describe: the client and the anti-CSRF token; approve or deny: the redirect

csrf_token.description: the consent anti-CSRF token (oauth_consent_csrf_token), returned once

redirect_to.description: the client's exact redirect with code (oauth_authorization_code), state and iss, or error access_denied, state and iss

The body is one of the two, never both.
